entries.appliesTo: covered entities — any county, city, town, village, school district, board of cooperative educational services, county vocational education and extension board, district corporation, SUNY, CUNY, or community college — using automated employment decision-making tools or AI systems

dutySources.documentation: § 6 (adding STL § 402-a) — 'any covered entity that utilizes an automated employment decision-making tool, shall publish a list of such automated employment decision-making tools on such covered entity's website'

sources.inventory: § 6 (adding STL § 402-a) — 'shall publish a list of such automated employment decision-making tools on such covered entity's website no later than the thirtieth of December next succeeding the date on which this section shall have become a law, and annually thereafter'
sources.appliesTo: § 4 (adding STL § 401(3)) — '"Covered entity" shall mean any county, city, town, village, school district, board of cooperative educational services, county vocational education and extension board, district corporation, the state university of New York, the city university of New York, or community college.'

flags: Not a duplicate: legiscan relation shows S 8831 'replaces' A 9487 — S 8831 is the surviving vehicle; A 9487 should be coded duplicateOf this bill.

Core of §§ 7-15 is anti-displacement/collective-bargaining protection fitting no listed duty: use of AI systems 'shall not result in the: (i) discharge, displacement or loss of position, including partial displacement such as a reduction in the hours of non-overtime work, wages, or employment benefits' and 'shall not affect the: (i) existing rights of employees pursuant to an existing collective bargaining agreement' — workforce-style protections applied to public employers (school districts, BOCES, SUNY, CUNY, community colleges, civil service).
The § 402-a disclosure duty is twice qualified by 'To the extent feasible', softening the annual-inventory obligation.

Bill also covers education entities (school districts, BOCES, SUNY, CUNY, community colleges); coded public-sector rather than education because coverage spans general local governments (counties, cities, towns, villages) and the civil service law.

§§ 1-3 and § 16 REPEAL provisions of the 2025 chapter (S. 7599-C / A. 8295-D), including Article 5 and § 103-f of the state technology law and § 115 of the education law; § 17 adds a sunset to that chapter: 'shall expire and be deemed repealed July 1, 2028'.

§ 18: most sections 'shall take effect on the same date and in the same manner as a chapter of the laws of 2025... as proposed in legislative bills numbers S. 7599-C and A. 8295-D, takes effect' — effectiveness is contingent on that chapter.
No penalty or enforcement provision in the text — exposure omitted (silence is silence).
